subject: COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB301. The prohibition is on ACCEPTING: a word ISO 8.9 reserves at edition E is refused in a user-defined-word slot AND in a system-name slot at E, and admitted at the editions 8.9 leaves it free. The gate is DERIVED, not listed - gen-cobol-words.ps1 computes it from reserved-words.json and CobolWordsDriftTests re-computes it independently, asserting set equality in BOTH directions and across BOTH halves (cobolWord under {userWordHere(W)}? and reservedGatedWord under its inverse), so neither a missing nor a stray gate survives. Words 8.9 reserves that the lexer never tokenizes are caught by the same funnel by NAME (measured: 01 LOCALE PIC X. at --std 2023 draws COBOL0901), so the rule holds over the whole 8.9 list and not merely over the token set. The corpus lanes carry both slots the rule names: pb301-screen-words-reserved-from-2002 declares the six words 8.9 adds in 2002 in a data-name slot AND puts CRT in the 12.3.7 implementor-name slot, and its acceptance complement at COBOL-85 is conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb301_screen_words_as_user_words_85; pb301-column-reserved-at-every-edition holds COLUMN, reserved at all four editions. Rule 3 of the same clause (context-sensitive words as user words) stays GAP - kb/Work PB655 class 4 measures 22 of them still refused (01 CAPACITY PIC X. at --std 2023 is a raw COBOL0001 today).
